external_entities.name: shoppers
external_entities.description: People who browse the storefront and place orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment status callbacks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders; it receives payment settlement webhooks and calls the order service.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that reads and writes orders and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: Shoppers browse the storefront through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Shoppers place orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service over gRPC when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read-write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four in orders-db.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.data_description: receipt, including which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a payment-settlement webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone to which the storefront API is exposed.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: third party
trust_boundaries.description: The separate-party zone containing the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because it serves the storefront and receives an HTTP POST webhook.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a storefront API used by shoppers and a POST callback to it.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because callers reach it through gRPC.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC; gRPC is an RPC interface rather than a web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The orders-db data is confidential because it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four in addition to orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains shopper addresses and card-last-four, which are personal and payment-related data.
